text: dsh-ai-memory 是把 DeepSeek Harness 会话接入 ai-memory 的插件：会话结束时调用 ai-memory 的 finalize-session，将已捕获的观察整理成可供其他 harness 检索的 wiki 页面。它监听 DSH 会话生命周期事件，并用分层定时扫描补齐异常结束的会话；同时跳过子 agent、串行处理并发结束事件、检查安装和捕获配置。适合已使用 ai-memory、希望 DSH 会话也进入共享记忆的用户。需要另行安装并运行 ai-memory，并配置 DSH 捕获 hooks；可选设置可调整 CLI 路径、数据目录和扫描行为。

dsh-ai-memory connects DSH sessions to ai-memory. It calls finalize-session to turn captured observations into searchable wiki pages, and periodically catches sessions left by unexpected exits. It skips child agents and checks setup. Install ai-memory separately and wire DSH capture hooks.
让 DSH 结束的会话也整理进 ai-memory 共享知识库。
怎样把 DSH 的会话记录变成其他编程助手能搜索的记忆？
DSH 会话结束后只留下观察记录，怎么触发总结归档？
我想让不同 coding harness 共用 DSH 产生的项目记忆。
DSH 被强制重启后，能自动补做未完成会话的整理吗？
如何避免子 agent 结束时把主会话记忆拆开？
Make completed DSH sessions searchable as shared ai-memory pages.
How can I finalize sessions left behind after DSH exits unexpectedly?
dsh-ai-memory 的功能「会话结束归档」：监听会话结束事件，将主会话排队交给 ai-memory finalize-session 整理。
dsh-ai-memory 的功能「异常退出补扫」：按启动后逐渐拉长的间隔扫描 SQLite 中闲置的 DSH 会话，分批补做归档。 由 DSH 生命周期事件或启动/定时流程触发，并调用本机 ai-memory CLI。
dsh-ai-memory 的功能「跳过子 agent」：读取会话标记并略过子 agent，避免把子会话独立归档。
dsh-ai-memory 的功能「启动环境诊断」：启动时检查 CLI、数据目录和 capture hooks，并记录缺项提示。
dsh-ai-memory 的功能「适配不同 shell 接口」：检测 shell API 能力，兼容 execute 与旧版 run 调用。
dsh-ai-memory 只负责归档已捕获的会话；还需单独安装运行 ai-memory，并在 DSH profile 配置 capture hooks，否则没有会话可供整理。

dsh-ai-memory README · dsh-ai-memory：**Memory bridge between DeepSeek Harness and ai-memory.**

[ai-memory](https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory) shares one memory across
20+ coding agents: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and more
all read and write the same wiki. DSH could only ever *read* it. This plugin
makes DSH a **full writer** too.

---

dsh-ai-memory README · What this is not：- **It is not ai-memory.** ai-memory is a separate project by a different
  author. This plugin does not contain it, does not bundle it, and does not
  replace it.
- **It is not a fork of ai-memory.** There is no shared code and no git
  relationship. ai-memory is written in Rust; this plugin is a single ~800-line
  JavaScript file that *calls* the `ai-memory` command-line program you install
  yourself. See [Credits](#credits).
- **It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by ai-memory's
  author.** It is an independent third-party integration.
- **It does not capture anything.** It only *finalizes* sessions that ai-memory
  has **already** captured. Capture comes from DSH hook wiring that you install
  separately — see [Prerequisites](#prerequisites).

dsh-ai-memory README · Credits：The memory engine this plugin drives is entirely the work of others:

> **[akitaonrails/ai-memory](https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory)** — MIT
> licensed. One Rust binary that captures agent sessions through lifecycle
> hooks, consolidates them into a searchable Markdown wiki, and serves that
> memory to 20+ harnesses over MCP and HTTP.

dsh-ai-memory README · Credits：**No ai-memory code is included here.** This repository contains zero lines
taken from that project. It is a DSH-side adapter that shells out to the
`ai-memory` binary, nothing more. If this plugin is useful to you, the credit
belongs upstream — please star their repository.

dsh-ai-memory README · Memory between harnesses：This is the point of the plugin, so it is worth stating precisely.

ai-memory is built on the idea that memory should follow *you*, not your editor.
Quit Claude Code mid-task, open Codex in the same directory, and the next agent
picks up a real handoff. That works because every harness writes into one shared
store, and session-end consolidation turns the raw record into readable wiki
pages the next agent can search.

dsh-ai-memory README · Memory between harnesses：DSH was the odd one out. ai-memory's consolidation is triggered by a **session
end** event, and DSH never fires one — its session-terminating path exits
through a signal that emits no disposal event at all. So DSH sessions landed in
ai-memory as raw observations and **stopped there**:

```
Claude Code session ends ──► consolidated ──► wiki page ──► readable by every harness
DSH session ends         ──► raw observations only ──► invisible to every harness
```

dsh-ai-memory README · Memory between harnesses：DSH could search the memory other agents wrote, but nothing DSH did ever became
memory the others could read. One-way, in the wrong direction.

This plugin closes that loop by firing the finalize step DSH never fires. With
it installed:

```
DSH session ends ──► this plugin ──► ai-memory finalize-session ──► wiki page
                                                                      │
              Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, … ◄────────────┘
```

dsh-ai-memory README · Memory between harnesses：A DSH session becomes a page that Claude Code can retrieve, that a teammate's
Codex can search, that shows up in the next agent's handoff brief. **DSH stops
being a read-only consumer of the shared memory and becomes a peer writer in
it.**

That is the whole value: not a new memory system, but one harness joining an
existing one properly.

dsh-ai-memory README · Prerequisites：Two things must already work. The plugin will not do either of them for you.

**1. A running ai-memory server with capture wired into DSH.**

dsh-ai-memory README · Prerequisites：Install ai-memory from [upstream](https://github.com/akitaonrails/ai-memory),
then wire DSH's lifecycle hooks so events are captured. ai-memory >=3.2.0
supports DSH natively; earlier versions need the legacy Claude Code bridge
configuration. A manual, single-command-string example supporting older servers
is in [`docs/hooks-dsh.json`](docs/hooks-dsh.json); see its native migration notes.

Verify capture independently before blaming this plugin:

dsh-ai-memory README · Prerequisites：```sh
ai-memory status          # sessions and observations should be increasing
ai-memory doctor          # inside your project directory
```

**2. The `ai-memory` CLI on the same machine.**

That is all. It resolves its own data directory and server URL, so the default
configuration needs no settings at all.

If the server is not running, this plugin logs a clear warning at startup and
does nothing else. Capture failing is a separate problem with a separate cause.

dsh-ai-memory README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-ai-memory
```

From GitHub instead of npm:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:rasyidmmz/dsh-ai-memory
```

Restart DSH afterwards. The loader imports plugin code without a cache-buster,
so an edited or newly added plugin is not picked up until the process restarts.

Confirm it loaded by searching the harness log for `ai-memory`:

dsh-ai-memory README · Install：```
[dsh-ai-memory] active v1.2.0 -- fast path session/disposed (zero idle cost) + ...
[dsh-ai-memory] preflight: ai-memory v3.1.1 | data_dir=... | server=127.0.0.1:49374
```

The preflight line is the fastest way to confirm the plugin found the same
ai-memory your hooks are writing to.

dsh-ai-memory README · From the DSH marketplace — the half this plugin does not bring：Installing from a marketplace gives you the **finalize** half in one row. Two
things are still yours to provide, and the startup log now names whichever one
is missing instead of looking merely idle:

dsh-ai-memory README · From the DSH marketplace — the half this plugin does not bring：1. **ai-memory itself.** The plugin shells out to the `ai-memory` binary; it does
   not bundle or install it. When the binary is missing the log says so, with the
   install link and the `exePath` key that overrides the expected location, and
   nothing is finalized until it appears.
2. **Capture hooks.** ai-memory only knows about a DSH session if DSH forwards
   lifecycle events to it. That wiring is one `insert:` row in the profile's
   `cordis.patch.yml` pointing `@deepseek-ai/dsh-hooks-claude-code` at a hooks
   file; the reference file ships in this package as
   [`docs/hooks-dsh.json`](docs/hooks-dsh.json). Without it ai-memory records no
   DSH sessions at all — so there is nothing to finalize, and the log says
   exactly that, with the path to that template.
section: From the DSH marketplace — the half this plugin does not bring

text:
dsh-ai-memory README · From the DSH marketplace — the half this plugin does not bring：The plugin deliberately does **not** write that row for you. The desktop
   profile reloads `cordis.patch.yml` live, so writing it from inside a running
   harness is how people hang their app; and a second hooks row sitting next to
   one you already have would capture every session twice.

When both are in place, the preflight is one line and the rest is silent.

plugin behaves identically with no `config:` block at all.

- insert:

dsh-ai-memory README · Configuration：| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `exePath` | Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ai-memory\ai-memory.exe`; elsewhere: `ai-memory` from `PATH` | Path to the ai-memory executable. |
| `dataDir` | unset | ai-memory data directory. **Leave unset** unless you use a non-standard location; the CLI then resolves its own, which is what the hooks use. |
| `agentKind` | stored session kind, falling back to `claude-code` | An explicit value pins finalization to that capture identity. Leave unset for mixed legacy/native stores. |
| `sweep` | `true` | The abandoned-session safety net. Set `false` to disable it entirely. |
| `preflight` | `true` | Log one line at startup naming the ai-memory version, data directory, and server it found. |
| `timeoutMs` | `120000` | Per-`finalize-session` timeout. |

dsh-ai-memory README · Legacy and native DSH capture：ai-memory **3.2.0** added `AgentKind::Dsh` and migration V85. Its DSH support is
now listed as **Hooks + MCP**. Earlier releases require `--agent claude-code`.
The UUID mapping is unchanged.

dsh-ai-memory README · Legacy and native DSH capture：A server upgrade does **not** change the identity written by existing hooks.
This plugin therefore reads each session's `agent_kind` from the local store
(read-only), accepting only `dsh` and `claude-code`. That identity stays fixed
through all project fallbacks and `--reopen`. Preflight never changes it.
The sweeper also excludes unrelated harness kinds before applying its existing
live-session, idle-time and UUIDv5 guards.

dsh-ai-memory README · Legacy and native DSH capture：If the row/store or `node:sqlite` is unavailable, finalization falls back to
`claude-code`, matching the shipped legacy hook template. For native capture on
a remote-only store, explicitly configure `agentKind: dsh`.

dsh-ai-memory README · Legacy and native DSH capture：To opt into native capture, first upgrade ai-memory to **3.2.0 or later**, then
change every capture command in your hooks file from `--agent claude-code` to
`--agent dsh` and restart DSH (the bridge reads hooks once). Start a new session
and verify its stored identity. Leave plugin `agentKind` unset so old captured
sessions can still finalize as `claude-code`. The plugin does not rewrite hooks,
relabel database rows, or modify your profile patch.
dsh-ai-memory README · How it works：Two paths, deliberately asymmetric.

dsh-ai-memory README · Fast path — an event, costing nothing while idle：When a session closes cleanly, DSH fires `session/disposed`. The plugin listens,
derives the session's stored UUID, and calls `ai-memory finalize-session`.

- **Idle cost: zero.** No timer, no query, no process started.
- **Reaction: immediate**, not waiting for a scheduled sweep.

It uses `session/disposed` rather than the two events that fire alongside it
because it is the only one carrying the full session object, so the working
directory is read directly instead of being cached or guessed.
section: Fast path — an event, costing nothing while idle

text:
dsh-ai-memory README · Safety net — the tiered sweeper：DSH terminates through `SIGTERM`, and `SIGTERM` fires **no** disposal event at
all. A session open at that moment is never finalized: it stays open forever
with no page. This is not hypothetical — one session with 459 observations was
left behind that way.

dsh-ai-memory README · Safety net — the tiered sweeper：So a sweeper exists that depends on no event: it reads ai-memory's store
directly and finalizes sessions that are provably dead. Its schedule is dense at
first and then eases off — 25s, 1 min, 3 min, 10 min, then every 30 min —
because the only case an event misses is a session abandoned by a restart, which
happens right when DSH starts.

dsh-ai-memory README · Safety net — the tiered sweeper：Guard 2 covers a second DSH window: that is a separate process, so its session
is invisible here, and without the delay it would be closed mid-write.

Guard 3 has a useful side effect worth knowing if you run DSH alongside real
Claude Code sessions in one repository: ai-memory stores those as version-4
UUIDs, so they can never be selected by this sweeper.

Set `sweep: false` to turn the whole net off; the fast path is unaffected.

dsh-ai-memory README · The seven traps this solves：Each of these broke an earlier version, and each fix is load-bearing. They are
worth listing because they are the reason a naive "just call finalize-session"
plugin does not work.

dsh-ai-memory README · The seven traps this solves：1. **The session id is not a raw UUID.** DSH ids look like `session-<uuid>` and
   ai-memory stores them as a derived UUID v5. Passing the raw string is
   rejected: `invalid uuid: invalid character: found 's' at 1`. Child agents use
   a bare UUID and must be passed *as is* — two id shapes, two treatments.
2. **The working directory must be explicit.** The shell service defaults to the
   DSH process's own directory, not the session's repository, so scope resolves
   to the wrong project.
3. **The project name is not always the folder's basename.** Hooks write it
   lowercased; the CLI derives it with original casing. Repositories without an
   `.ai-memory.toml` marker only match after a lowercase retry.
4. **No `2>&1`.** DSH runs commands with stderr unredirected, and collapsing it
   inside the command fails there, exiting non-zero having done nothing.
5. **Subagent detection must read the session header, not the registry.** The
   agent registry deletes an entry *before* announcing its disposal, so a
   registry lookup is always empty — including for the main session. An earlier
   version used it as a filter and therefore skip

dsh-ai-memory README · Troubleshooting：All output is prefixed `[dsh-ai-memory]`. Search the harness log for it.

The prefix deliberately is not `[ai-memory]`: ai-memory has its own logs, and an
identical prefix makes it impossible to tell whose line you are reading.

dsh-ai-memory README · Troubleshooting：| Log line | Meaning | Action |
|---|---|---|
| `active v1.1.0 ...` | Plugin loaded | — |
| `preflight: ai-memory vX \| data_dir=...` | Found the server | Confirm the data directory matches your hooks |
| `WARNING: ai-memory executable not found` | Wrong `exePath` | Set `exePath` in config |
| `preflight: the ai-memory server did not answer` | Server not running | Start ai-memory |
| `sandbox runner is broken (0xC0000142)` | DSH's sandbox runner is failing under Electron; the plugin switched to the unconfined path | See "Sandbox runner" below. Sessions still finalize |
| `session ... -> page created` | Working | — |
| `session ... -> no open session matched` | Already finalized, or never captured | Check `ai-memory status`; if observations are not rising, the **hooks** are the problem, not this plugin |
| `session ... FAILED` | The CLI returned an error | The message tail is included |
| `sweeper could not read the store` | ai-memory's schema changed | The fast path keeps working; only the safety net is down |
| `sweeper: no abandoned sessions` | Normal, most sweeps | — |

dsh-ai-memory README · Troubleshooting：If nothing appears at all, the plugin is not loaded — check the profile's
`cordis.patch.yml` and restart DSH.

> **Note on `finalize-session` and consolidation.** This plugin calls
> `finalize-session`, which is a client of the running server. It does not
> invoke an LLM and does not write wiki pages itself; the server does that. If
> pages are not appearing, check the server's own logs.

dsh-ai-memory README · Compatibility：- **DSH**: developed and tested against DSH Desktop **`0.2.1-rc.2`**
  (the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop` package), Node 24. Re-verified on 0.2.1-rc.2
  on 2026-10-18 from the installed `app.asar`: `agent/created`,
  `agent/disposed` and `session/disposed` are still emitted, `ctx.sessions.get()`
  still returns a session whose `header` carries `cwd`, `origin` and
  `delegationDepth`, and `ctx.shell` still exposes `execute()` only (the
  `run()`-then-`execute()` capability branch below covers both). 1.0.4 and
  1.1.1 were verified on `0.2.0-rc.2`.

dsh-ai-memory README · Compatibility：> Earlier revisions of this README said "DSH Desktop 0.9.1". That was wrong —
  > no such DSH version exists. `0.9.1` had been read off an unrelated
  > changelog; the package version at the time was `0.1.7-rc.2`. Revisions
  > 1.0.0-1.0.3 were tested on `0.1.7-rc.2`.

dsh-ai-memory README · Compatibility：- **ai-memory**: developed against **2.5.2** (upgraded from 2.4.0 through
  2.5.2, each verified working end-to-end), re-verified on **3.1.1** on
  2026-10-18. What was actually checked, not assumed:
  - `finalize-session` still accepts `--agent`, `--workspace`, `--project`,
    `--session-id`, `--reopen` and `--json`;
  - its output lines are unchanged — `Finalized …` on success and
    `No open … sessions matched …` when there is nothing to close, which is
    what this plugin's classification reads;
  - session ids are still `uuid5(NAMESPACE_OID, native id)`
    (`crates/ai-memory-core/src/ids.rs:94`), the exact mapping
    `sessionIdToUuid` reproduces;
  - a 2.6-era store opens under 3.1.1: it migrated to schema **V83** without
    error, and the sweeper's query returns the same rows afterwards;
  - `status --json` still exists and still reports `version`, `data_dir` and
    `bind`, which the startup preflight prints.
  `--reopen` and the marker's `identity` key arrived in 2.5.0 and are used by
  1.1.0+. See the compatibility notes below for what the upgrades changed.
- **Platforms**: Windows is the tested platform. Linux and macOS command

dsh-ai-memory README · Upgrading the ai-memory *server* from 2.x to 3.x：The CLI contract this plugin uses did not change, but the **server** may refuse
to start after the jump, and that failure looks like the plugin's fault because
finalize calls then fail with a connection error. Observed on the author's
machine going 2.6.0 → 3.1.1 against a copy of the store:

```
provider not configured: no openai-oauth token found at <data-dir>\auth.json;
run `ai-memory auth login openai-oauth`
```

dsh-ai-memory README · Upgrading the ai-memory *server* from 2.x to 3.x：2.6.0 was serving with an `openai-compat` provider configured through
`llm_base_url` plus environment keys; 3.1.1 wants a credential file for that
provider route. The **store migrated cleanly** (schema V83, same pages,
sessions and observations) — so this is a provider/auth step, not data loss.
Run the `ai-memory auth login …` command the message names (or point the config
at a still-valid `api_key_env`) before restarting the service, then check
`ai-memory status` again.

dsh-ai-memory README · ai-memory 2.4.0 → 2.4.1：The upgrade was run and verified on the author's machine; nothing broke. The
store kept every page, session and observation, and embeddings improved
(6 pages missing → 0). Two entries in that release are worth knowing here:

dsh-ai-memory README · ai-memory 2.4.0 → 2.4.1：- **CRLF pages are read correctly again** — a page saved by a Windows editor
  used to load without its frontmatter (`pinned` / `expires_at` silently lost).
  Relevant on Windows, which is the tested platform.
- **Session ids no longer split on letter case** — `D:\…\Default Project` could
  become two separate projects. On an affected store, this release merges them.

dsh-ai-memory README · Two shell API shapes：The plugin calls `ctx.shell` through one helper that accepts **both** shapes:

| Harness | Call | Result |
|---|---|---|
| older | `shell.run(spec)` | `{ exitCode, stdout, stderr }` |
| DSH 0.1.7-rc.2 | `shell.execute(spec)` | handle, then `handle.result()` |

dsh-ai-memory README · Two shell API shapes：This is detected by capability (`typeof ctx.shell.execute`), never by version
number, so a future rename cannot silently break it again. It matters because
`PwshLocalExecutor` in 0.1.7-rc.2 exposes **only** `execute()`: without the
branch, every finalize dies with `shell.run is not a function` — and because the
failure only reaches the log, it looks like "the plugin is loaded but nothing
happens" rather than an error.

dsh-ai-memory README · Sandbox runner：DSH 0.1.7-rc.2 launches its sandbox runner through Electron, and the confined
child process dies with `STATUS_DLL_INIT_FAILED` (`0xC0000142`). Measured
directly, same command, correct SID:

| Launcher | Result |
|---|---|
| `node.exe` + runner | `exit=0` (works) |
| `DeepSeek Harness.exe` + runner | `exit=3221225794` (`0xC0000142`) |

A plugin's `ctx.shell` calls carry no session, so they fall back to the default
`workspace-write` policy and always take the broken path.

dsh-ai-memory README · Sandbox runner：The plugin therefore tries the **normal, confined** path first and falls back
only when it sees `0xC0000142`, remembering the switch. The moment DSH fixes its
runner, finalize returns to being sandboxed with no change needed here.

dsh-ai-memory README · Sandbox runner：**Be aware of the trade-off:** the fallback widens the CLI call's permissions
beyond the workspace (`danger-full-access`). It is contained to the
`ai-memory finalize-session` invocation — not the agent's own tools — and the
plugin never writes files itself. If that is not acceptable in your setup, do not
run it on a harness with a broken runner; there is no config switch to disable
the fallback in 1.0.2.

dsh-ai-memory README · If ai-memory changes：The plugin reads ai-memory's SQLite store directly in **one** place, the
sweeper, and only to *find* abandoned sessions. If a future ai-memory release
changes that schema, the sweeper logs an error and stops; the fast path is
untouched because it uses no SQL at all. Set `sweep: false` to silence it
entirely in that case.
